Radish and Quesillo Tamales

Served at: La Noche de Rabanos

Makes 12-15 tamalesPrep 45 minCook 1 hour 30 min

La Noche de Rábanos (Night of the Radishes) is a cherished Oaxacan festival where colossal radishes are transformed into breathtaking sculptures, admired for their artistry rather than their flavor. While these carving radishes are not typically consumed, tamales remain a beloved and traditional food enjoyed throughout the festive season in Oaxaca. This recipe offers a unique, modern interpretation, incorporating the crisp, peppery bite of edible radishes into a savory tamale filling, celebrating the spirit of the radish in a delicious, unconventional way.

Ingredients

  • 12-15 dried corn husks, soaked in hot water for at least 30 minutes
  • 2 cups (240 g) masa harina for tamales
  • 1 ½ teaspoons baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup (240 ml) vegetable broth, warm
  • 1 cup (225 g) lard or vegetable shortening, softened
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1 cup (150 g) red radishes, finely diced
  • ½ cup (75 g) white onion, finely diced
  • 1 jalapeño, seeded and minced (optional, for mild heat)
  • ½ teaspoon salt (for filling)
  • 4 ounces (115 g) Oaxaca cheese (quesillo), shredded or crumbled

Method

  1. Prepare the corn husks: Place dried corn husks in a large bowl, cover with hot water, and weigh down with a plate to keep them submerged. Let them soak for at least 30 minutes, or until pliable.
  2. Make the filling: Heat olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add finely diced radishes and onion, sautéing until softened, about 5-7 minutes. If using, add minced jalapeño and cook for another 2 minutes. Season with ½ teaspoon salt. Remove from heat and let cool completely. Once cool, gently mix in the shredded Oaxaca cheese.
  3. Prepare the masa: In a large bowl, whisk together masa harina, baking powder, and 1 teaspoon salt.
  4. In a separate bowl, beat the softened lard or shortening with an electric mixer on medium-high speed until light and fluffy, about 3-5 minutes.
  5. Gradually add the dry masa mixture to the creamed lard, alternating with the warm vegetable broth, mixing until a soft, uniform dough forms. The masa should be light and spreadable. To test, drop a small piece of masa into a glass of cold water; if it floats, it's ready.
  6. Assemble the tamales: Take a softened corn husk, pat it dry, and spread about 2-3 tablespoons of masa evenly over the wider end of the husk, leaving a border of about 1 inch (2.5 cm) on the sides and bottom, and 2-3 inches (5-7.5 cm) at the top.
  7. Place about 1-2 tablespoons of the radish and cheese filling in the center of the masa.
  8. Fold one side of the corn husk over the filling, then fold the other side over to overlap. Fold the narrow bottom end of the husk up towards the center. Leave the top open.
  9. Arrange tamales upright in a steamer basket, open end facing up. Do not pack them too tightly, allowing steam to circulate.
  10. Steam the tamales: Place the steamer basket in a large pot with about 2 inches (5 cm) of water, ensuring the water does not touch the tamales. Bring water to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover tightly, and steam for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, or until the masa separates easily from the husk. Check water level periodically and add more hot water if needed.
  11. Serve: Carefully remove tamales from the steamer. Let them rest for 5-10 minutes before unwrapping and serving warm.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, you can use chicken broth instead of vegetable broth in the masa.
  • If Oaxaca cheese is unavailable, use mozzarella or a mild white cheddar.
  • To vary the filling, consider adding finely chopped cooked chicken or pork carnitas along with the radish and cheese.
